stories.headline: Google releases Gemma 4 12B, an encoder-free multimodal open model that runs on 16GB laptops

key_facts.fact: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an 11.95B-parameter dense encoder-free multimodal model under Apache 2.0 on June 3, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are introducing Gemma 4 12B, our latest model designed to bring agentic multimodal intelligence directly to laptops... Open and accessible: Released under an Apache 2.0 license with support across the developer ecosystem.

key_facts.fact: The 12B model uses no separate vision or audio encoders, projecting raw image patches and audio waveforms directly into the LLM embedding space via lightweight linear layers.
key_facts.excerpt: The Gemma 4 12B Unified model has no separate vision or audio encoder. Instead, raw image patches and audio waveforms are projected directly into the LLM's embedding space through lightweight linear layers.

key_facts.fact: Gemma 4 12B has a 256K-token context window and is small enough to run locally with just 16GB of VRAM or unified memory.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemma 4 12B Unified | 11.95B dense, encoder-free | 256K | base, IT

key_facts.fact: Google's broader Gemma 4 family scores 89.2% on AIME 2026 (31B model) and 86.4% on tau2-bench retail agentic tool use, with benchmarks approaching the 26B MoE on the 12B variant.
key_facts.excerpt: AIME 2026 Mathematics | No tools | 89.2%... tau2-bench Agentic tool use | Retail | 86.4%

key_facts.fact: Google also released macOS versions of AI Edge Gallery and a new AI Edge Eloquent on-device voice dictation app to run Gemma 4 12B locally.
key_facts.excerpt: Generate code in AI Edge Gallery (new to Mac) • Dictate and edit text via Google AI Edge Eloquent.

stories.headline: Altman, Amodei, Hassabis, Suleyman urge Congress to mandate synthetic DNA screening

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman (OpenAI), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), Demis Hassabis (Google DeepMind), Mustafa Suleyman (Microsoft AI), and Alexandr Wang (Meta) signed an open letter calling for mandatory federal screening of orders for synthetic nucleic acids and the equipment to make them.
key_facts.excerpt: As life sciences researchers, builders of AI and biotechnology, and experts with a wide range of views on how to approach AI policy, we call on legislators to make screening of orders for synthetic nucleic acids — and the equipment needed to make them — mandatory.

key_facts.fact: Signatories also include Nobel laureates David Baker and Martin Hellman; the letter says AI systems now outperform PhD-level virologists on lab procedure questions.
key_facts.excerpt: Signatories include Sam Altman (OpenAI), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), Demis Hassabis (Google DeepMind), Mustafa Suleyman (Microsoft AI), and Nobel laureates David Baker and Martin Hellman... AI systems now outperform PhD-level virologists on questions about lab procedures, raising the risk of misuse.

key_facts.fact: The letter asks providers of synthesized DNA to check requests against sequences of concern, verify customer legitimacy, and keep records so threats can be traced back to the source.
key_facts.excerpt: It asks providers of synthesized DNA and manufacturers of synthesis machines to check synthesis requests for sequences of concern and to verify customer legitimacy before shipping orders. Providers should also record synthesis orders and sequence data to support legitimate biosecurity investigations.

key_facts.fact: The letter urges Congress to act this session and asks states to base requirements on existing federal and industry guidelines to avoid a patchwork of conflicting laws.
key_facts.excerpt: Congress should act this session, and we applaud the legislative efforts currently underway. To ensure a consistent national standard rather than a patchwork of conflicting laws, states should also consider implementing requirements based on existing federal and industry guidelines.

stories.headline: OpenAI publishes blueprint pushing mandatory CAISI evaluations and state-law preemption for frontier AI

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published 'A blueprint for democratic governance of frontier AI' on June 3, 2026, proposing that the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) conduct mandatory pre-deployment evaluations of the most capable frontier models.
key_facts.excerpt: Once CAISI has sufficient technical expertise and operational capacity, policymakers should require the most capable frontier models to undergo a CAISI evaluation before public release.

key_facts.fact: The blueprint diverges from President Trump's June 2 executive order, which lodged a classified covered-frontier-model benchmark with the NSA and CISA and bars any mandatory licensing or preclearance requirement.
key_facts.excerpt: Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize the creation of a mandatory governmental licensing, preclearance, or permitting requirement for the development, publication, release, or distribution of new AI models, including frontier models.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says CAISI should conduct evaluations and recommend mitigations but not approve or block deployments, and developers should be free to deploy if CAISI misses a statutory timeline.
key_facts.excerpt: CAISI's role should be to conduct evaluations and recommend mitigations—not to approve or block deployments... If CAISI fails to complete an evaluation within the defined time period due to bandwidth, hardware, personnel, or other constraints, developers should be permitted to deploy without penalty.

key_facts.fact: The blueprint calls for federal preemption of state safety laws (referencing California SB 53, New York's RAISE Act, and Illinois SB 315) and treats recursive self-improvement as an urgent priority for CAISI monitoring.
key_facts.excerpt: It also calls for a federal framework similar to SB 315, and for preemption of 'state laws that seek to regulate the same frontier safety risks.' Notably, the blueprint has a huge focus on recursive self-improvement, saying that CAISI should 'treat RSI as an urgent priority'.

stories.headline: Bezos leads $500M raise for Flourish, hunting the brain's 'core algorithm' for efficient AI

key_facts.fact: Flourish closed a $500M funding round at a $2.5B valuation, with Jeff Bezos leading the investment, according to WIRED.
key_facts.excerpt: With $500 million in funding and a reported $2.5 billion valuation, Flourish wants to reinvent AI by putting real neurons under the microscope.

key_facts.fact: Flourish was founded by Thomas Reardon, who built Internet Explorer at Microsoft and previously sold neural-interface startup CTRL-labs to Meta for up to $1 billion in 2019.
key_facts.excerpt: Thomas Reardon, who created Internet Explorer and sold neural interface startup CTRL-labs to Meta for up to $1 billion, is raising approximately $500 million for Flourish at a $2.5 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: The startup studies connectomics (neural connections in the brain) to design AI architectures that are radically more energy-efficient, targeting the architectural layer above silicon rather than building new chips.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup uses connectomics and neuroscience to design AI architectures that are radically more energy-efficient, targeting the architectural layer above silicon rather than building new chips. Lux Capital and GV, who backed CTRL-labs, are expected to lead the round.

key_facts.fact: The human brain runs on about 20 watts, while leading AI systems require megawatts; closing this efficiency gap is Flourish's stated goal.
key_facts.excerpt: While the human brain runs on about 20 watts, leading AI systems need megawatts. Closing this efficiency gap is Flourish's main goal.

stories.headline: Generalist AI raises $400M at $2B valuation led by Radical Ventures for robot foundation models

key_facts.fact: Generalist AI, a robotics startup, raised $400 million at a $2 billion valuation in a round led by Radical Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: Generalist AI, a robotics startup, has raised $400 million in a new funding round... The financing, set to be announced on Thursday, values Generalist at $2 billion, including the money raised. Radical Ventures led the round.

key_facts.fact: Participating investors included 8VC, Union Square Ventures, Hanabi Capital, plus existing backers Nvidia and Bezos Expeditions.
key_facts.excerpt: Radical Ventures led the round with participation from venture firms 8VC, Union Square Ventures and Hanabi Capital, as well as existing investors Nvidia Corp. and Bezos Expeditions.

key_facts.fact: The company was founded by Pete Florence, Andy Zeng, and Andy Barry; team members previously worked at OpenAI, Boston Dynamics, and Google DeepMind on PaLM-E, RT-2, and Gemini Robotics.
key_facts.excerpt: Our team of researchers, roboticists, and company builders come from OpenAI, Boston Dynamics, Google DeepMind, and other frontier labs... we pioneered large embodied multimodal models and vision-language-action models (PaLM-E, RT-2, Gemini Robotics).

key_facts.fact: Generalist released its GEN-1 embodied foundation model in April 2026 and is a founding member of Nvidia's Cosmos Coalition alongside Skild AI and Agile Robots.
key_facts.excerpt: Generalist AI: Known for its strict conviction in training large parameter counts entirely from scratch, Generalist AI has joined the coalition... continuing the push for 'intelligent improvisation' seen in their recent GEN-1 model rollout.

stories.headline: Nvidia acquires Kumo AI for at least $400M to expand enterprise predictive models

key_facts.fact: Nvidia acquired Kumo AI for at least $400 million, according to The Information; Kumo's three co-founders have already transitioned to Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia didn't disclose the terms of the acquisition, but the deal has already been finalized, according to reports by Fortune and The Information... Josifovski and his co-founders Hema Raghavan and Jure Leskovec have already transitioned to the chipmaker.

key_facts.fact: Kumo builds foundation models that make predictions on structured enterprise data (customer, payment) using graph machine learning techniques developed by its Stanford-pedigreed founders.
key_facts.excerpt: Kumo AI has developed AI models that answer predictive questions based on structured enterprise data such as customer information and payment data... Kumo combined synthetic data with graph machine-learning technology developed by Stanford University founders.

key_facts.fact: Kumo had previously raised $37 million from Sequoia Capital and others in 2022 at a $250 million valuation, per PitchBook, and counts Reddit, DoorDash, Databricks, and Snowflake as customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Mountain View, California-based Kumo had raised $37 million in venture capital funding via two rounds, which both took place in 2022, with the most prominent investor being Sequoia Capital. Its customers include Reddit Inc., DoorDash Inc. and the U.K. grocery chain J Sainsbury plc.

key_facts.fact: Kumo released its latest model, KumoRFM-2, in April 2026; the deal adds to Nvidia's recent string of acquisitions, including a reported $20B Groq acqui-hire and Illumex for around $75M.
key_facts.excerpt: Kumo released its latest model, KumoRFM-2, in April this year, and counts DoorDash, Reddit, Databricks and Snowflake as customers and partners.

stories.headline: Lila Sciences in talks for $2B Series B at $8.5B valuation, anchored by CalPERS and Nvidia

key_facts.fact: AI-for-science startup Lila Sciences is in talks to raise about $2 billion at a pre-money valuation of about $8.5 billion, per Bloomberg.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial intelligence research startup Lila Sciences Inc. is in talks to raise about $2 billion at an expected valuation of about $8.5 billion before the new money, according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The Series B financing is anchored by the California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) and Nvidia's venture arm NVentures.
key_facts.excerpt: The Series B financing is anchored by the California Public Employees' Retirement System and Nvidia Corp.'s NVentures.

key_facts.fact: Lila closed a $350 million Series A in October 2025 at a >$1.3B valuation, after a $200M seed; its valuation roughly 6x's in eight months on AI-discovery promises.
key_facts.excerpt: Lila Sciences said in October that it had closed a $350 million Series A, bringing its valuation to above $1.3 billion. The company emerged from stealth mode last year after a $200 million seed round.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2023 by Flagship Pioneering (the incubator behind Moderna), Lila is building 'AI Science Factories' — automated robotic labs running experiments driven by its models — and claims early proof of concept generating novel antibodies and carbon-capture materials.
key_facts.excerpt: Lila Sciences was founded in 2023 by Flagship Pioneering, the same incubator that launched 2015 No. 1 CNBC Disruptor 50 company Moderna... Lila is building out AI Science Factories — automated robotic labs that can continuously run experiments... Lila has already demonstrated early proof of concept, generating novel antibodies and developing new carbon capturing materials.
